context: Independent offline claim verification; inspected only the mechanically whitelisted claim set and cited original raw sources. No role reports, raw claims, adjudication, lead draft, prior answers, network, browser, or source edits.
context_start_limit: Start is the first recorded verifier clock observation; dispatch itself was not separately timestamped.
snapshot_identity_status: Supplied enclosing snapshot identity; not interpreted as a per-file digest and not independently recomputed in this pass.
severity_policy: Supplied severity strings retained unchanged; no comparative winner, independent ranking, or hidden rubric.
refutation_policy: The filtered input supplied no explicit refutation fields. No refutations were removed; qualifications and source tensions are recorded per claim.

claims.statement: The target prescribes clicking Back; this does not prove the contracted sequential keyboard traversal and Enter activation.
claims.evidence: Target line 10 says “Click Back”. Contract transitions[6] instead specifies traversal Tab and activation Enter; checker lines 35–36 requires sequential keyboard traversal and Enter. The project back-focus invariant expressly says a click or programmatic focus does not prove keyboard reachability.
claims.limits: This establishes an instruction/evidence gap in the fixture, not a deployed keyboard defect. The project invariant is corroboration from an inspected original source.

claims.statement: The target omits the summary Space-close and Enter-reopen steps present in the contract.
claims.evidence: Target lines 7–8 proceed directly from opening help to reaching Close. Contract transitions[3] and [4] prescribe summary Space to close, then summary Enter to reopen.
claims.limits: The target also leaves the initial summary activation unspecified, while contract transitions[2] specifies Enter. This corroborating omission does not change the supplied severity or scope of this claim.

claims.severity: High conditional impact; omission Medium in QA report
claims.statement: The target has no pre-navigation read-only/origin guard or blocked-analytics evidence instructions; no actual policy violation has been observed.
claims.evidence: The complete target lines 5–10 contains no request-method guard, navigation-origin guard, or blocked-analytics recording instruction. Contract scope permits GET/HEAD/OPTIONS, limits[2] requires retaining blocked analytics effects, and project invariants[2] explicitly requires blocking other methods and off-origin main-frame/popup navigation.
claims.limits: “Pre-navigation” is an operational ordering inference needed to protect initial navigation, not a quoted timing requirement. No live observation was performed, so the absence of an observed incident is an evidence limit, not proof that no incident exists.

claims.statement: Close restores summary focus while Back restores introduction-heading focus; these are separate obligations.
claims.evidence: Contract transitions[5].focus_after is summary, while transitions[6].focus_after is introduction-heading. Checker lines 32–34 enforces these distinct destinations. Project close-focus invariant explicitly requires separate verification.
claims.limits: These are acceptance obligations. Neither the contract nor checker establishes current focus behavior in a browser.

claims.statement: Use forward sequential Tab then Enter for canonical Close and Back. Checker tolerance of Shift+Tab for Back does not amend the literal Tab transition or validate Close traversal.
claims.evidence: Both literal contract transitions[5] and [6] use traversal Tab and activation Enter. Checker lines 35–36 accepts either Tab or Shift+Tab only for Back; it does not inspect Close traversal or Close activation.
claims.limits: Forward Tab as the canonical test is a sourced planning decision matching the literal contract. It is not a claim that Shift+Tab is forbidden: the project Back invariant expressly permits Tab or Shift+Tab. Checker tolerance does not rewrite the JSON transition.

claims.severity: High if guard weakened; no observed incident
claims.statement: Scope permits only GET, HEAD, OPTIONS and no answers; expected blocked analytics must retain observed effects.
claims.evidence: Contract scope.answer_policy is unanswered and allowed_methods is GET/HEAD/OPTIONS. Limits[0] prohibits answers, results, and submission; limits[2] says “An analytics POST is expected to be blocked; retain its observed effects.” Project invariants[2] requires blocking all other methods and recording blocked analytics without relaxing policy.
claims.limits: Expected analytics is a declared expectation; no request, blocking event, or user-visible effect was observed in this offline pass. “Retain” applies to observed effects, which must not be invented.

claims.statement: Contract and observation policy currently agree on https://qaizen.io as their sole allowed origin.
claims.evidence: surface-contract.json.allowed_origins and observation-policy.json.allowed_origins each contain exactly one identical value: https://qaizen.io.
claims.limits: “Currently” refers to the supplied snapshot only; no remote policy or deployed origin behavior was checked.

claims.statement: The checker reads contract JSON only, cannot validate Markdown or deployed keyboard behavior, and expressly limits its result to contract consistency.
claims.evidence: The checker main routine parses json.loads(Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text(...)) and passes that object to validate. Its return explicitly states “Contract consistency only; browser observations establish current behavior.” There is no Markdown or browser processing.
claims.limits: This conclusion follows from reading the entire checker, not just the cited return/main lines. No checker execution was needed for this source-code claim, and no exit result is asserted.

claims.severity: Low in Delivery; Medium in Architecture
claims.statement: The target is a reconstructed fixture; acceptance expectations and historical baseline are not evidence of current website pass or defect, and private commits do not identify deployment.
claims.evidence: Target line 3 explicitly identifies a newly authored reconstructed tutorial fixture and disclaims website-defect evidence. Contract provenance says expectations are acceptance obligations, not evidence that current deployment passed, and locates the proof gap in the protocol rather than the website. Limits[3] states private commits do not identify deployment.
claims.limits: The baseline date is a supplied provenance field, not independently verified historical browser evidence. Nothing here certifies a present website pass or defect.

claims.statement: TASK requests a plan for the target using original project sources, with outputs outside inputs and no supplied input or skill edits.
claims.evidence: TASK.md requests planning changes to target/verification-protocol.md using the three original project sources; calls the tutorial a target rather than authority; requires outputs outside inputs; prohibits editing supplied input or skill resources and using prior reports or network answers.
claims.limits: This verifies the supplied task scope. This verifier only wrote the two requested output artifacts and did not execute the broader planning task.

claims.severity: Medium ambiguity; High potential guard violation
claims.statement: Current profile requires origin guards for main-frame/popup navigation and method guards for all requests. Original allowlists do not explicitly resolve comprehensive third-party subresource authorization; no permission is inferred.
claims.evidence: Project invariants[2] explicitly covers all non-GET/HEAD/OPTIONS requests and off-origin main-frame/popup navigation. Contract and observation policy provide origin lists but no explicit comprehensive third-party subresource authorization rule.
claims.limits: This is an open boundary, not a new permission or a finding that third-party requests are permitted. Method restrictions apply to all requests. The sources do not settle whether additional origin restrictions should cover every subresource.

claims.statement: Interpret returned question/help absence at the visible, accessible and interactive presentation boundary, without requiring DOM deletion or questionnaire re-entry. Actual markup remains unknown.
claims.evidence: Target line 10 requires the introduction visible and question/help absent. Contract names returned-introduction as the destination and maps introduction-heading to h1. Neither source requires DOM deletion or questionnaire re-entry.
claims.limits: The proposed visible, accessible, and interactive presentation boundary is an interpretation, not an explicit source requirement. Sources do not define “absent” or supply markup. Avoid claiming accessibility-tree removal, hidden-control inertness, DOM removal, or re-entry behavior as verified facts. The proposal can be adopted as a planning decision with that qualification.
